Cc: Tina Lopez <t.lopez@auditfirm.io>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request — VM evidence for SIG/SOC2 review

Hi Irene,

Audit team flagged a gap in our supplier pack: they need a concise packet showing Redwood's vulnerability management rhythm and your SLA commitments for CVE remediation (critical/important/medium). Specific asks:
- Scan cadence (unauthenticated vs authenticated; agents vs network tooling) and last 6 months sample results
- SLA commitments by severity and exception handling process
- A map of artifacts that satisfy SIG/CAIQ items (evidence files)
- An owner attestation for the timeline to closure for open CVEs (if any)

Can you send this by end of week? Tina from our SOC2 vendor is cc'd — she may have format preferences.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Director of Infrastructure Risk
BluePeak Financial

---
(attachment: request_summary.pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Tina Lopez <t.lopez@auditfirm.io>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — VM evidence for SIG/SOC2 review

Alex / Tina — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Markus (SecOps) and Laura (Compliance) to assemble artifacts. High level now:

- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated agent scans for hosts in prod, weekly external network scans, monthly container image scans, quarterly full-application dynamic scans. We also run targeted scans daily for critical release windows.
- SLAs: Critical (CVSS >=9.0) — remediation or compensating control within 7 business days; High (7.0-8.9) — 30 calendar days; Medium (4.0-6.9) — 90 calendar days. Exceptions go through our risk-acceptance flow with documented compensating controls and a patch window.
- Evidence mapping: we'll provide a table that maps SIG/CAIQ controls to artifacts: scan exports, patch manifests, change-request IDs, and the cve-closure log.
- Owner attestation: SecOps will provide a signed attestation (PDF) confirming the SLA commitments and the current open CVE list with expected closure dates.

I'll attach a compact playbook and the cadence matrix for initial review; Markus will finalize the cve-closure spreadsheet.

Action items: Markus — please attach cve-closure-log and note any CVEs with exceptions. Laura — prepare a short attestation paragraph we can sign. Alex/Tina — let us know if you want an alternate mapping format (CSV vs. XLSX).

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

(attachments: redwood_vm_playbook_v1.3.pdf, scan-cadence-matrix.csv)

- Snapshot summary: 12 open items total: 1 critical (CVE-2026-1458) — in remediation with patch scheduled for 2026-09-15 (canary on 09-13); 4 high, 7 medium. All high/critical tracked on the patch calendar and change requests filed.
- Validation artifacts: authenticated-scan-exports (last 6 months), external-scan-exports, image-scan-report (monthly), and deployment manifest change-IDs for the fixes. Links are in the Drive folder.
- Exceptions: one medium has a compensating control (WAF rule) applied; documented in the exception sheet and signed by engineering manager.

Attestation (draft):
"Redwood Inference attests that the vulnerability management program described in the attached playbook and cadence matrix is in active operation. Remediation SLAs are as stated in our playbook. The listed CVEs in cve-closure-log-20260909.xlsx reflect current open items; expected closure dates are indicated and owned by SecOps."

Irene / Laura — please review and if acceptable I'll convert to a signed PDF and put the final artifacts in the shared Drive link. Alex / Tina — let us know if you need the exports in a different hash-signed format for your audit.

Regards,
